title: Contentment
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Contentment is the grace-shaped confidence that God is enough and that His care is trustworthy in both abundance and need. It is not passivity, but settled trust in God’s sufficiency.
summary: Contentment is the grace-shaped confidence that God is enough and that His care is trustworthy in both abundance and need. It is not passivity, but settled trust in God’s sufficiency.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the believer’s greatest treasure and sufficiency. Because believers belong to Him, they can learn contentment without being ruled by possessions, circumstances, comparison, or lack.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Contentment is learned. Paul knew how to be brought low and how to abound because his strength was in the Lord. Contentment does not depend on perfect circumstances, but on trust in God’s provision and presence.

Scripture warns that the love of money and craving for more can pierce the soul with many sorrows. Contentment resists the lie that peace will come only when circumstances change or possessions increase.

Christian contentment is not indifference to suffering or laziness in responsibility. It is confidence that God will never leave His people and that His grace is sufficient in weakness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Discontentment often grows through comparison, fear, entitlement, or disappointment. It can make people blind to God’s present care while chasing what cannot satisfy.

This doctrine gives peace to both the needy and the comfortable. Christ is enough when life is lean, and He remains enough when life is full.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your desires and complaints before God honestly. Reject comparison, receive daily provision with gratitude, and seek first the kingdom of God. Learn to say with faith that the Lord is your Shepherd and that His grace is sufficient for today.
